eventMetadata.context_description: Mexico City's June climatology features daytime highs typically peaking near 24–25°C due to its 2,240-meter elevation, which reduces surface heating compared with lower-altitude sites. On June 12, 2026, the market-implied odds reflect this narrow range because model guidance and recent observations show borderline conditions: ample morning insolation under partly cloudy skies could push readings to 25°C, while earlier or stronger convective development—common in the onset of the rainy season—would cap the peak at 24°C through increased cloud cover, reduced solar input, and evaporative cooling from showers. Official forecasts indicate 24–25°C highs with scattered afternoon thunderstorms and 15–25 mm rainfall possible, creating uncertainty around the exact timing of cloud build-up that separates these two outcomes. Historical analogs from early June show similar split probabilities when instability indices are moderate, and traders are weighting the latest high-resolution model runs that remain closely divided on whether maximum temperatures breach 25°C before convection intensifies.

**Forecast models for Ankara on June 13, 2026, currently cluster around a daily maximum near 21–23 °C, producing the tight 33.5 % / 33.5 % split between the “21 °C or below” and “22 °C” outcomes.**

Recent runs show increased cloud cover and scattered thundery showers, which limit daytime heating compared with the seasonal June average of roughly 25–28 °C. Key drivers include a modest northerly flow advecting slightly cooler maritime air and modest mid-level moisture that favors convective development rather than strong insolation. Ensemble spreads remain modest but straddle the 21–23 °C range because small differences in shower timing, cloud thickness, or boundary-layer mixing can shift the peak by 1–2 °C.

Higher-probability bins above 24 °C receive little market weight because current guidance shows no strong warm advection or clearing trend before the diurnal maximum. The market therefore prices the narrow band of forecast outcomes that official and private models are still resolving, with the two leading contracts reflecting genuine uncertainty in the final 1 °C increment.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Official NWS guidance and ensemble model runs currently point to a high near 78°F for Denver on June 13 under mostly sunny skies with light northerly winds shifting easterly, keeping afternoon mixing modest and limiting peak downslope warming.**  

This aligns closely with mid-June climatological normals (82–83°F) while reflecting a modest cool bias from a weak trough and potential for scattered high clouds or early convection that could trim insolation. Traders have concentrated bets in the 78–81°F bins because short-range models (GFS/ECMWF) show only small spread in 500 mb heights and surface dewpoints, with uncertainty mainly around exact wind direction and boundary-layer mixing that can add or subtract a few degrees.  

Broader context includes the seasonal outlook for above-average temperatures across the Front Range, but this day-specific setup favors near-normal readings rather than the hotter ridge-dominated pattern seen earlier in the month. Upcoming afternoon model updates and NWS area forecast discussions will likely refine the exact ceiling as steering flow and moisture profiles evolve overnight.

**Market-implied odds favor a June 14 high of 24–26°C in Paris, with 25°C leading at 37% followed by 26°C at 25% and 24°C at 19.5%.** These probabilities align with the latest short-range model consensus and observed trends as of June 12. High pressure building over western Europe is promoting mostly clear to partly cloudy skies and gradual warming, while Atlantic influences and typical early-summer boundary-layer mixing keep daytime maxima from surging higher.

Ensemble guidance from sources such as ECMWF, GFS, and Météo-France shows afternoon highs clustering near 24–26°C under light to moderate northwesterly flow, with lows in the low-to-mid teens. Some deterministic runs reach 29–31°C under stronger insolation, but these are outliers given modest ensemble spread and recent run-to-run consistency around the mid-20s. Historical June climatology (average highs near 22–24°C) further anchors expectations, and the absence of an established heat dome or southerly flow reduces the chance of extremes above 28°C.

Traders are pricing the narrow forecast window and upcoming model updates—particularly the next Météo-France and ECMWF runs—as the key drivers. Any shift in cloud cover, wind direction, or boundary-layer depth over the next 48 hours could move probabilities among the 24–26°C bins, which together hold over 80% of the market.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Current forecasts from models and the Taiwan Central Weather Administration point to a highest temperature in Taipei on June 14 likely in the 28–29°C range, with afternoon thundershowers and persistent cloud cover suppressing peaks below the June climatological average of 30–32°C.** 

Short-range guidance shows highs near 28.3°C (83°F) under overcast skies and scattered convective activity, typical of the early summer transition when monsoon moisture fuels brief but effective cooling showers. Ensemble spread remains tight around this band because steering patterns and boundary-layer humidity favor widespread cloudiness rather than full insolation. 

Traders have clustered probability on 28°C and 29°C (each ~23.5%) because these align with the latest model consensus; outcomes at 30°C or higher would require clearer skies and stronger surface heating than currently indicated, while cooler readings depend on heavier or earlier rainfall. Key variables to watch include updated CWA guidance on shower timing and any shifts in low-level flow that could alter cloud cover or the urban heat-island contribution.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Masroor Airbase Station in degrees Celsius on 14 Jun '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Masroor Airbase Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/pk/karachi/OPKC.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from the Pakistan Meteorological Department and models indicate Karachi's maximum temperature on June 14 will likely fall in the 34–36°C range, aligning with the market's heaviest positioning on 35°C. The city's coastal location exposes it to persistent Arabian Sea onshore flow and sea breezes that typically cap daytime highs below inland peaks, even during pre-monsoon heat. Current conditions show elevated heat indices above 50°C from humidity, but no strong subsidence or wind shift appears imminent to push readings to 37°C or higher. Historical June averages hover near 35–36°C, with recent observations confirming moderation around this level absent major synoptic changes. Updated model runs and PMD briefings through mid-June remain the key near-term catalysts.
